content.value_statement: Error handling often becomes inconsistent across services and languages. This skill guides clear exceptions, Result types, retries, and fallbacks for reliable applications.
actual_capabilities: Compares exceptions, Result types, error codes, and Option patterns.
Provides Python, TypeScript, Rust, and Go error handling examples.
Guides retry logic, exponential backoff, and circuit breaker design.
Shows graceful degradation and fallback strategies for service failures.
Helps design custom error classes, messages, and propagation rules.
limitations: Does not run diagnostics, tests, or live service checks by itself.
Examples require adaptation before use in production code.
Does not replace language-specific framework documentation or security review.
Does not guarantee correct recovery behavior for every distributed system.

use_cases.title: Standardize API Errors
use_cases.description: Design consistent error categories, messages, and propagation rules for an application programming interface.

use_cases.title: Improve Service Resilience
use_cases.description: Add retry, timeout, circuit breaker, and fallback patterns to reduce cascading failures.

use_cases.title: Review Error Handling Quality
use_cases.description: Identify swallowed errors, broad catches, unclear messages, and missing cleanup paths before release.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review the error handling in my function. Identify missing validation, unclear messages, and simple recovery options. Keep the advice language-specific.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single function or small feature.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Error Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an error model for my API. Include error categories, exception or Result choices, and user-safe messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for a service boundary or public interface.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Distributed Reliability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add retry, timeout, circuit breaker, and fallback guidance for this service workflow. Explain where each pattern belongs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reliability planning for networked systems.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Migration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to migrate inconsistent error handling across Python, TypeScript, Go, and Rust services. Provide a staged plan and verification checklist.

output_examples.input: A TypeScript API returns null on lookup failures and logs every parse error.
output: Recommended a not found error for missing records and a typed parse failure for invalid input.
Suggested logging only at the boundary that handles the failure.
Added user-safe messages and developer-focused context fields.

output_examples.input: A payment workflow fails when the payment provider times out.
output_examples.output: Suggested timeout limits, safe retry rules, circuit breaker thresholds, and a fallback response for customers.

output_examples.input: A Rust service needs to replace panic-prone parsing.
output_examples.output: Mapped expected failures to Result values, preserved parse context, and added validation before downstream calls.

best_practices: Choose explicit error types for expected failures and reserve crashes for unrecoverable bugs.
Preserve context while keeping user-facing messages safe and clear.
Verify recovery paths with tests, observability, and failure simulation.
anti_patterns: Catching broad exceptions without a clear recovery action.
Swallowing errors or returning silent defaults that hide failures.
Logging the same failure at every layer before rethrowing it.

faq.question: What languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It includes patterns and examples for Python, TypeScript, Rust, and Go.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it choose between exceptions and Result types?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains tradeoffs and recommends patterns based on expected and unexpected failures.

faq.question: Can it help with distributed systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers retries, circuit breakers, graceful degradation, and fallback strategies.

faq.question: Does it run code or call external services?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but it does not execute code or make network requests.

faq.question: How should teams use the examples?
faq.answer: Teams should adapt the examples to their frameworks, error policies, and test coverage.
